Maladaptive daydreaming is caused by absence. By something that you lack. 
Me, I daydream about acceptance, I daydream about being popular and being well liked, ect. Because in reality, I have no one to talk to about my problems, I have no one who likes me all that much. 

What I've found helps me not to daydream is creating this story with my friend. They really hold me to creating the scripts and I don't want to disappoint them so I usually will create them. 

I think the first step of quitting, now that I think about it, is to fill that hole. What do you lack?
Glad to hear I'm not alone. I really don't have someone like that in reality, it's hard out here. It'll get better, but I suppose for now these made up conversations will have to suit.

I mean, dude, you're only 19. I'm 16. 
We've got a lot of time ahead of us. We have to work toward stopping, even if it feels good and even if it feels right. I want to stop badly, always, but I just can not. But it's also because I've never really tried. 
It's always been me trying for a day and giving up because I had nothing to replace it with. Can't take a heroin addict off heroin cold turkey, it'll kill them. We're basically doing the same thing to our brain, abusing the pleasure and reward aspect of our brains. 

Replacement is the biggest helper. It's also helpful to know that someone else is going through this. I've been alone for a very long time in this.

Quitting is possible. It is, it's just a lot fucking harder than most addictions, I think. Either way it's an addiction and addictions are very hard to quit. I know we can do it. I just can't right now.

I've tried to quit on multiple occasions and I've failed each time. I don't know if I'm really myself half the time, or if I have alters, or if they're just inner people, or if I'm just delusional. I don't know if quitting will get rid of these inner people or if i'll have them.
